title: Toward Training Superintelligent Software Agents through Self-Play SWE-RL
data_curation: SSR's central data contribution is to eliminate human-curated training data: it assumes only a corpus of pre-built Docker images containing source repositories with dependencies installed, with no access to issue descriptions, existing tests, test runners, test parsers, or language-specific infrastructure. The bug-injection agent must itself discover how to run tests and build a parser. All training tasks are self-generated bug artifacts (bug_inject.diff, test_script.sh, test_files.txt, test_parser.py, test_weaken.diff) validated by execution-based consistency checks (test existence/coverage, parser validity, script validity, bug validity, test-weakening validity, inverse mutation testing). Failed solver attempts are recycled into 'higher-order' bugs (up to second order) to expand the distribution. Training and the baseline RL share identical CWM environment images. Evaluation uses SWE-bench Verified (500 human-verified issues) and SWE-Bench Pro public split (731 tasks), one attempt each, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, with ~2% paired standard error.
curriculum: SSR's curriculum is the self-play loop itself, online and evolving rather than fixed. A single shared policy alternates between bug-injection and bug-solving roles; the bug distribution naturally tracks the agent's current capability, so static bug-generation pipelines cannot match it. Control parameters (min_changed_files, min_passing_tests, min_failing_tests) tune bug complexity. Two injection strategies are compared—removal-only (delete code hunks/files) and removal+history (revert git-log changes)—with the latter giving the best curriculum. Failed initial solver attempts seed higher-order bugs (capped at second order to avoid overlap), introducing layered, interdependent edits resembling real development. Training runs 150 global steps (~2.5B tokens) with 30-step LR warmup to 3e-6, building on the CWM-sft 32B pre-RL checkpoint. Ablations show full self-play beats both injection-only and repair-only (which uses frozen prior-run bugs), confirming that an evolving, jointly-trained task distribution is essential for sustained improvement.
method: SSR (Self-play SWE-RL) trains one LLM policy in two coupled roles—bug-injector and bug-solver—on the same containerized codebase with Bash/editor tools (CWM scaffold). The injector produces a validated bug artifact; the solver sees only the reversed test-weakening patch as a formal spec and must emit a repair patch. Rewards: r_solve is binary (+1 if all tests pass, -1 otherwise); r_inject = -1.0 on consistency failure, -alpha (alpha=0.8) for degenerate solve rates s in {0,1}, and 1-(1+alpha)s for 0<s<1, pushing the injector toward challenging-yet-solvable bugs near the solver's frontier. Both signals jointly update shared weights. The RL stack reuses async CWM-RL with 'large-batch/small-staleness' settings (ScaleRL/MiniRL-inspired): 512 H100s (64 train, 448 rollout), 131K-token context, 16M-token global batch, group size 8, rollouts discarded after >8 off-policy steps. A theoretical challenger-solver analysis identifies dominant/tunnel-vision strategies and motivates grounding and shallow self-play as mitigations.
eval_metrics: Evaluation is on SWE-bench Verified (500 human-verified real GitHub issues) and SWE-Bench Pro public split (731 enterprise-level tasks), measured by resolve rate (patch passes fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass tests via a parser-driven pipeline), one attempt per problem, temperature 1.0/top-p 0.95, no test-time scaling. Headline: SSR shows clear self-improvement of +10.4 points on SWE-bench Verified and +7.8 on SWE-Bench Pro, and consistently outperforms the human-data baseline RL (same images and hyperparameters, but given issue descriptions and test suites) across the entire training trajectory, generalizing to natural-language issues unseen in training. Ablations (averaged over 1231 tasks) show self-play > repair-only > injection-only; removal+history > removal-only > direct-injection (direct collapses to trivial one-line bugs); solver feedback in the inject reward gives only a slight, largely negligible gain. Evaluation noise is ~2% paired standard error.
key_results: SSR (CWM-sft 32B base) achieves +10.4 points self-improvement on SWE-bench Verified and +7.8 on SWE-Bench Pro, consistently beating the human-data baseline RL throughout training while using no human-labeled issues or test suites. Full self-play also beats both repair-only and injection-only ablations.
evolution_note: SSR extends the 2025 agentic-SWE-RL wave (SWE-RL, DeepSWE, CWM) and corpus-grounded self-play (SPICE, Absolute Zero, R-Zero) by removing human-curated issues/tests entirely, framing bug injection/repair as a self-play game over real repositories. It is an early step toward open-ended, self-improving software agents but flags unresolved scaling instability and reward-hacking risks that later work must address.
